checks.action: Save the control stream as plain text (ASCII).
checks.question: Is the control stream a readable, non-empty text file?

checks.action: NM-TRAN reads ASCII only; replace typographic quotes, dashes, µ and non-breaking spaces.
checks.question: Is the file free of a byte-order mark and of non-ASCII characters?

checks.action: Save the file with one kind of line ending.
checks.question: Are the line endings consistent (all CRLF or all LF)?

checks.action: Split long lines: lists ($INPUT, $TABLE) over several lines, code with `&` continuations.
checks.question: Are the lines within the line-length limit?

checks.action: Replace tabs by spaces; some NM-TRAN versions and editors treat them differently.
checks.question: Is the file free of tab characters?

checks.action: Remove the spaces at the ends of the lines.
checks.question: Is the file free of trailing white space?

checks.action: Each problem is checked on its own.
checks.question: How many problems ($PROBLEM records) does the file hold?

checks.action: Begin the file with $PROBLEM and a short description.
checks.question: Does the control stream start with $PROBLEM (after $SIZES and comments)?

checks.action: Correct the misspelt record name.
checks.question: Is every record name one that NM-TRAN knows?

checks.action: Abbreviations of three or more letters work, but full names are clearer.
checks.comment: every record name written in full
checks.question: Are the record names written in full (not abbreviated)?

checks.action: Merge the duplicated $INPUT, $DATA, $SUBROUTINES, $PK, $ERROR, $PRED, $DES or $MODEL records.
checks.comment: each single-use record at most once
checks.question: Is each single-use record given at most once per problem?

checks.action: Add the missing record.
checks.question: Are the records the model needs present ($INPUT, $DATA, a model, $THETA)?

checks.action: Use $PRED alone, or $SUBROUTINES with $PK and $ERROR.
checks.question: Is the model either $PRED or PREDPP ($SUBROUTINES with $PK and $ERROR), not both?

checks.action: Reorder the records; NM-TRAN applies $ESTIMATION options in order and some tools expect this layout.
checks.question: Are the records in a usual order ($INPUT and $DATA before the code, parameters before $ESTIMATION, $ESTIMATION before $COVARIANCE and $TABLE)?

checks.action: Fill in the empty record or remove it.
checks.question: Does every record that needs content have it?

checks.action: Move $SIZES to the top of the file.
checks.question: Is $SIZES (when present) before $PROBLEM?

checks.action: Correct the path or create the file.
checks.question: Do the files named by $INCLUDE, $MSFI and $ETAS/$PHIS FILE= exist?

checks.action: Rename the label.
checks.question: Are the $INPUT labels valid names (a letter first, letters, digits and _, within the length limit)?

checks.action: Rename or DROP the duplicate.
checks.question: Are the $INPUT labels unique?

checks.action: Add the missing data item.
checks.comment: the needed data items are present
checks.question: Are the data items NONMEM needs in $INPUT (ID and DV; TIME and AMT for PREDPP)?

checks.action: Rename the column.
checks.question: Are reserved names kept out of the $INPUT labels (THETA, ETA, EPS, PRED, RES, WRES …)?

checks.action: Keep the item (remove =DROP) or stop using it in the code.
checks.comment: dropped items are not used in the code
checks.question: Are DROPped data items left out of the code (they stay usable in IGNORE/ACCEPT)?

checks.action: Add EVID (and MDV) to the dataset and $INPUT for clarity, especially with several dose and observation types.
checks.question: Are EVID and MDV given, or can NONMEM infer them?

checks.action: Check that every label sits over the right column; renaming in $INPUT is allowed but easy to get wrong.
checks.question: Do the $INPUT labels match the dataset header (number and names)?

checks.action: Add =DROP to the label of each text column (or recode it as numbers).
checks.question: Are the dataset columns that hold text DROPped in $INPUT?

checks.action: Correct the path in $DATA.
checks.question: Does $DATA name a dataset that exists (relative to the control stream)?

checks.action: Add IGNORE=@ (skips lines that start with a letter or @), or IGNORE=# with a # header.
checks.question: Will the IGNORE option skip the header line of the dataset?

checks.action: Correct the condition.
checks.question: Do the IGNORE/ACCEPT conditions use $INPUT labels and valid operators, without mixing IGNORE=(list) and ACCEPT?

checks.action: Combine conditions, or filter the dataset beforehand.
checks.question: Is the number of IGNORE/ACCEPT conditions within NONMEM's limit?

checks.action: Correct CMT in the dataset or the compartments of the model.
checks.comment: every CMT value exists in the model
checks.question: Do the dataset's CMT values exist in the model?

checks.action: Add the missing columns or remove the extra labels.
checks.question: Does the dataset have at least as many columns as $INPUT has labels?

checks.action: Run `nlmx qc-data` on the dataset for the full data checks.
checks.comment: 1000 records read of 1000 data lines, 100 individuals
checks.question: How many records and individuals will NONMEM read after IGNORE/ACCEPT?

checks.action: Start such lines with the IGNORE character (or a letter with IGNORE=@), or remove them.
checks.question: Are the dataset lines that are not data (comments, notes, a second header) skipped by the IGNORE option?

checks.action: Use .EQN./.NEN. for numeric comparisons, or write the value exactly as in the file.
checks.comment: the conditions match the values as written
checks.question: Do .EQ./.NE. conditions on numbers match the dataset as intended (they compare text: 0 is not 0.0)?

checks.action: Check the label and the value of the condition; a condition that matches nothing is probably mistyped.
checks.comment: every condition selects records; observations remain
checks.question: Does every IGNORE/ACCEPT condition select some records, and do observations remain?

checks.action: Choose a TRANS supported by the ADVAN.
checks.question: Is the ADVAN known and the TRANS valid for it?

checks.action: Add TOL=n to $SUBROUTINES.
checks.question: Is TOL given for the general ADVANs (6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 15)?

checks.action: Add $MODEL with the compartments, and $DES with the differential equations.
checks.question: Does a general ADVAN have $MODEL, and an ODE ADVAN $DES?

checks.action: Assign them in $PK (e.g. CL and V for ADVAN1 TRANS2).
checks.comment: the required PK parameters are assigned
checks.question: Are the basic PK parameters required by ADVAN/TRANS assigned in $PK?

checks.action: Set S1 (or S2 …) so that F is a concentration, e.g. S2 = V2 or S2 = V2/1000.
checks.question: Is the scale S of the observation compartment set in $PK?

checks.action: Correct the compartment number.
checks.question: Do the compartment numbers of Fn, ALAGn, Rn, Dn, Sn and A(n) exist in the model?

checks.action: Write one DADT(n) for each compartment of $MODEL.
checks.question: Does $DES define DADT(n) for every compartment, and for no other?

checks.action: Correct the statement shown.
checks.question: Does the abbreviated code parse (syntax)?

checks.action: Close every block IF with ENDIF and every DO WHILE with ENDDO.
checks.question: Are IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF and DO WHILE/ENDDO balanced?

checks.action: Use THETA(1) … THETA(n) for the n values of $THETA; remove unused ones or FIX them.
checks.comment: THETA indices match $THETA, every THETA used
checks.question: Are the THETA(n) indices within $THETA, and is every THETA used?

checks.action: Use ETA(1) … ETA(n) for the n random effects of $OMEGA.
checks.comment: ETA indices match $OMEGA, every ETA used
checks.question: Are the ETA(n) indices within $OMEGA, and is every ETA used?

checks.action: Use EPS(1) … EPS(n) for the n random effects of $SIGMA.
checks.comment: EPS indices match $SIGMA, every EPS used
checks.question: Are the EPS(n)/ERR(n) indices within $SIGMA, and is every EPS used?

checks.action: Define the variable earlier, add the column to $INPUT, or correct the spelling.
checks.comment: every variable is defined before use
checks.question: Is every variable defined before it is used (or a data item or NONMEM name)?

checks.action: Define Y in $ERROR (PREDPP) or $PRED.
checks.question: Is Y defined in $ERROR (PREDPP) or $PRED?

checks.action: Guard them, e.g. IF (IPRED.LE.0) IPRED = 1E-10, or W = SQRT(…) with a floor.
checks.question: Are LOG, SQRT and divisions protected against zero or negative values?

checks.action: Rename the variable.
checks.question: Are the variable names valid (within the length limit, not reserved words)?

checks.action: Move the statement to the right record.
checks.comment: each block uses what it may
checks.question: Does each block use only what NONMEM allows there (no EPS in $PK, DADT only in $DES, A(n) not in $PK)?

checks.action: Write MU_n = LOG(TVPAR) and PAR = EXP(MU_n + ETA(n)) for faster, more stable EM estimation.
checks.question: Are MU-referencing statements present for the EM and Bayesian methods?

checks.action: Use the variable, add it to a $TABLE (e.g. IPRED, IWRES, individual parameters), or remove it.
checks.comment: every variable is used or tabulated
checks.question: Is every variable defined in $PK, $ERROR, $PRED or $DES used later or written to a $TABLE?

checks.action: Correct the record.
checks.question: Do $THETA, $OMEGA and $SIGMA parse?

checks.action: Write (lower, initial, upper) with lower < initial < upper.
checks.comment: every initial value strictly inside its bounds
checks.question: Are the THETA bounds ordered, with the initial value inside them?

checks.action: Move the initial value inside; an estimate starting on a bound may not move.
checks.comment: initial values away from the bounds
checks.question: Are the THETA initial values away from their bounds?

checks.action: Start at a non-zero value; a zero initial value cannot be scaled.
checks.question: Are the estimated THETAs started away from zero?

checks.action: Give a positive variance, or FIX a zero.
checks.question: Are the diagonal OMEGA/SIGMA values positive, and zeros FIXed?

checks.action: Reduce the covariances (|correlation| < 1).
checks.question: Are the OMEGA/SIGMA blocks positive definite?

checks.action: Correct the number of values.
checks.question: Does each BLOCK(n) have n(n+1)/2 values, and does SAME follow a block of the same size?

checks.action: Check the scale of the variance (variance, not CV or SD, unless SD is written).
checks.question: Are the OMEGA initial values plausible (CV between 1 % and 300 %)?

checks.action: Drop the bounds of a FIXed THETA.
checks.question: Are FIXed THETAs written without bounds that would be ignored?

checks.action: Add $ESTIMATION METHOD=1 INTERACTION (or the method you need).
checks.question: Is there an $ESTIMATION (or $SIMULATION) record?

checks.action: Correct the option (INTERACTION and LAPLACIAN need METHOD=1).
checks.question: Are the methods and options of $ESTIMATION valid together?

checks.action: Add INTERACTION to $ESTIMATION METHOD=1.
checks.comment: INTERACTION where the error model needs it
checks.question: Is INTERACTION set when the residual error depends on the prediction?

checks.action: Add MAXEVAL=9999 so the search does not stop early.
checks.question: Is MAXEVAL given for the classical methods?

checks.action: Use METHOD=1 LAPLACIAN (and LIKELIHOOD/-2LL where needed).
checks.question: Do likelihood models (F_FLAG, LIKELIHOOD, -2LL, M3) use LAPLACIAN?

checks.action: End an SAEM or BAYES chain with IMP EONLY=1 for an objective function value.
checks.question: Is the sequence of methods sensible (an EM method followed by IMP or an evaluation)?

checks.action: Add $COVARIANCE (e.g. PRINT=E UNCONDITIONAL) for standard errors.
checks.question: Is a $COVARIANCE step requested?

checks.action: Add POSTHOC to $ESTIMATION METHOD=0.
checks.question: Does FO (METHOD=0) have POSTHOC when tables or code need individual estimates?

checks.action: Check the spelling of the option.
checks.question: Are the $ESTIMATION and $COVARIANCE options known?

checks.action: Give each $TABLE its own FILE=.
checks.question: Are the $TABLE file names unique?

checks.action: Correct or remove the item.
checks.question: Is every $TABLE item a data item, a variable of the code or a NONMEM output?

checks.action: Add ONEHEADER NOPRINT for readable table files.
checks.question: Do the $TABLE records use ONEHEADER and NOPRINT?

checks.action: Add an sdtab-style $TABLE.
checks.question: Is there at least one $TABLE with the diagnostics (ID, TIME, DV, PRED, IPRED, CWRES)?

checks.action: Remove the repeated item.
checks.question: Is each item listed only once per $TABLE?

checks.action: Add FILE=name (e.g. sdtab1) to the $TABLE.
checks.comment: every NOPRINT table has a file
checks.question: Does every $TABLE with NOPRINT have FILE= (otherwise the table is written nowhere useful)?

checks.action: Describe the model on the $PROBLEM line.
checks.question: Does $PROBLEM carry a description?

checks.action: Label each value, e.g. (0, 5) ; CL (L/h).
checks.question: Are the THETA, OMEGA and SIGMA values labelled with comments?

checks.action: Add a ;; header with the run, purpose, author and date.
checks.question: Does the file have a header comment (description, author, date)?
